back: People of working age who are employed or unemployed and actively seeking work (the economically active population).
People of working age not working and not seeking work: students, homemakers, the retired, the long-term sick, discouraged workers.

front: Give five factors affecting the size of the labour force.
back: Population size and age structure; school-leaving age; retirement age; women's participation; migration; health; job opportunities; government policy.

front: Give three factors affecting the composition of the labour force.
back: Education and training; government policy; the structure of the economy; migration (brain drain).

front: Give four ways of controlling population growth.
back: Family planning; education of girls; better healthcare to cut infant mortality; raising the marriage age; incentives; awareness campaigns.

front: What is the usual textbook definition of working age?
back: About 15 to 64 years; statistics offices may use other limits, so check the official definition.

front: How does raising the school-leaving age affect the labour force?
back: It reduces its size in the short run but raises its skills and productivity in the long run.
